fact: Vanguard reports the NDPC National Commissioner saying the Nigeria Data Protection Act, enacted in June 2023, mandates the Commission to decide the adequacy of other countries' data protection as a basis for cross-border transfer of personal data, and that the Commission approves binding corporate rules, codes and certification mechanisms for such transfers.

The Official Gazette text of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023, signed 12 June 2023, lists in its contents a Part VIII on cross-border transfers of personal data (sections 41 to 43: basis for transfer, adequacy of protection, other bases for transfer outside Nigeria); the captured text stops at the contents and gives no provision wording.
Premium Times reports the Commission found Meta transferred Nigerians' data abroad without authorisation under the Nigeria Data Protection Act and ordered it to stop transfers without approval.

Premium Times reports the Commission's 18 February 2025 orders against Meta, including a $32.8 million fine, cited transfer of data abroad without authorisation and directed it to halt such transfers without approval.
